title: Seed sounds on the petals
hook: anatomy posters label organs; this old map writes letters on its petals
carry: in a mantra, the sound itself is sacred
tomorrow: a moon on the left, a sun on the right. what runs between?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the chakras as a map rose to the crown, a lotus of a thousand petals: at the crown, Shakti and Shiva are one. Today, a closer look at those petals.

Anatomy posters label things: thighbone, artery, nerve. The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana labels its map too, but strangely. Each lotus along the spine has letters of the Sanskrit alphabet set on its petals. At its center sits a shape and a seed sound, and inside, a god and a goddess. No one has ever drawn an organ like that. So why would a map of the body carry an alphabet?
screen: `ANATOMY POSTERS LABEL ORGANS.` → `THIS MAP WRITES LETTERS ON PETALS.` → `WHY AN ALPHABET?`

segments.voice: Because it isn't a map of the body's parts. It's a map for the mind on the way up, and it's built of sound. That's one of Hinduism's oldest convictions: sound itself can be sacred. The Vedas were kept for centuries by ear, memorized syllable by syllable, because how they sounded mattered as much as what they meant. A mantra works the same way: it's said for its sound, not only translated. Here each lotus has a bija at its center, a seed syllable. The text gives the root lotus lam, and the throat lotus ham. They aren't words with a dictionary meaning. They're seeds, said inwardly. And many tantric teachers call the letters of the alphabet matrika, little mothers, forms of the Goddess herself. So the letters on the petals aren't labels. They're the climb, sounded out. Here's the line worth taking to dinner: the old map is drawn with an alphabet, not a scalpel. Some modern writers have tried to line the lotuses up with glands or bundles of nerves. The old map never asked for that. Read on its own terms, the puzzle solves itself. Letters on petals means this is a place for the mind to rest, and listen.
screen: `LETTERS ON EVERY PETAL.` · `SOUND ITSELF CAN BE SACRED.` · `BIJA: LAM AT THE ROOT, HAM AT THE THROAT.` · `MATRIKA: THE LETTERS AS LITTLE MOTHERS.` · then, large: `A PLACE TO REST, AND LISTEN.`

segments.voice: Sit tall. Say Om slowly, out loud, three times, letting each one fade before the next. Then say it inwardly, once with each out-breath, for the rest of the sit. If Om isn't yours to say, hum one low, steady note instead, and listen to it end.
The chakras as a map: lotuses with letters on their petals and a seed sound at the center, drawn for the mind, not for the scalpel.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: For the road: in a mantra, the sound itself is sacred. The old map is drawn with an alphabet. Until tomorrow, then.

screen: `DAY 1647 COUNTS.` → `THE TANTRAS, FRAMED · 39 OF 42.` → `TOMORROW: A MOON, A SUN, AND WHAT RUNS BETWEEN?`

howItsDone: Many Hindus chant Om and other mantras aloud or inwardly; in tantric meditation on the chakras, practitioners picture each lotus with its petals and letters and repeat its seed syllable inwardly, as the texts describe and a teacher guides.
